# The Shepherd Who Names the Stars

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name. Great is our Lord and mighty in power; his understanding has no limit." — Psalm 147:4-5

## Reflection
On a clear autumn night, far from city lights, the sky can hold nearly three thousand visible stars. Yet astronomers estimate our galaxy alone contains over one hundred billion—each one numbered, each one known. In the ancient world, shepherds watched these same skies, guiding their flocks through the darkness. They knew each animal by name, noticing when one wandered or grew weak.

David, himself a shepherd, wrote that God numbers the stars and calls them each by name. Think of it—the One who spoke galaxies into being also knows the exact count of every flaming sun, and not one is anonymous to Him. If God tends the cosmos with such intimate attention, how much more does He tend you?

Autumn reminds us that seasons change and fields grow bare. The nights stretch longer. Perhaps you feel small beneath that vast expanse, wondering if your life matters amid such immensity. But the God who names the stars has also written your name on His heart. His understanding has no limit—and it includes every detail of your story.

You are not lost in the dark. You are known, counted, and held by the Shepherd of the stars.

## Prayer
Lord of the cosmos, You spoke the stars into being and call each one by name. Thank You that Your care extends to me—that I am not forgotten or overlooked. When the nights feel long and I feel small, remind me that Your understanding has no limit and Your love has no end. Guide me through this season as a shepherd guides the flock, and let me rest in the truth that I am fully known and deeply loved. Amen.
